modern: What will he do? He will sanctify us completely; see the verse before. He will carry on the work of making us pure until we are perfect in every part. He will preserve our “whole spirit, and soul, and body, blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.” He won’t let us fall from grace or come under the rule of sin. What great favors these are! We may well adore the Giver of such gifts, too great for words.

Who will do this? The Lord who called us out of darkness into his marvelous light, out of death in sin into eternal life in Christ Jesus. Only he can do it: perfection and preservation like this can come only from the God of all grace.

Why will he do it? Because he is “faithful”: faithful to his own promise, which is pledged to save the believer; faithful to his Son, whose reward it is that his people will be presented to him faultless; faithful to the work he has begun in us by our effectual calling. The saints don’t rely on their own faithfulness, but on the Lord’s own faithfulness.
Come, my soul, here is a grand feast to begin a dull month with. There may be fog outside, but there should be sunshine inside.

notes.term: Faithful is he that calleth you, who also will do it
notes.note: [[1Thess.5.24|1 Thessalonians 5:24]].
Make holy; set apart for God. The verse before is Paul’s prayer: “And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly” ([[1Thess.5.23|1 Thessalonians 5:23]]).

notes.term: Out of darkness into His marvelous light

notes.note: Christ “is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory” ([[Jude.1.24|Jude 1:24]]).
Effective; actually doing what it sets out to do. Effectual calling is God’s inward call that actually brings a person to faith, not only an outward invitation.
November, the month of London’s thick fogs.

modern: The Lord may hold back many pleasant things, but “no good thing.” He is the best judge of what is good for us. Some things are certainly good, and these we may have for the asking, through Jesus Christ our Lord.
Holiness is a good thing, and he will freely work it in us. Victory over evil leanings, strong tempers and bad habits he will gladly give, and we shouldn’t go on without it.

He will give full assurance, and close communion with himself, and access into all truth, and boldness that prevails at the mercy-seat. If we don’t have these, it’s because we lack the faith to receive them, not because God is at all unwilling to give. A calm, heavenly frame of mind, great patience and warm love: he will give all of these to holy diligence.

But note well that we must “walk uprightly.” There must be no mixed motives or crooked dealings, no hypocrisy or deceit. If we walk dishonestly, God can’t give us favors, for that would be a reward for sin. The way of uprightness is the way of heavenly wealth: wealth so great it includes every good thing.
What a promise to plead in prayer! Let’s get down on our knees.

notes.term: No good thing will he withhold

notes.note: Being fully sure of your salvation. “Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith” ([[Heb.10.22|Hebrews 10:22]]).
Close fellowship and sharing, with God or with each other.
Prevailing with God in prayer: asking and receiving.
The gold lid of the ark of the covenant, where God met with his people; a picture of coming to God in prayer.
Lack.
A state of mind.
Aims that work against each other; here, saying one thing while aiming at another.
Dishonestly, wickedly.
A bonus or reward for sin.

modern: Mercy may seem slow, but it’s sure. The Lord, in his unfailing wisdom, has set a time for his gracious power to go into action, and God’s time is the best time. We’re in a hurry; the vision of the blessing stirs our desire and speeds up our longing; but the Lord will keep his appointments. He is never early, and he is never late.

God’s word is spoken of here as a living thing that will speak and will come. It is never a dead letter, as we’re tempted to fear when we have watched a long time for it to come true. The living word is on its way from the living God, and though it may seem to linger, it isn’t really doing so. God’s train isn’t running late. It’s only a matter of patience, and we’ll soon see the Lord’s faithfulness for ourselves. No promise of his will fail: “it will not lie.” No promise of his will be lost in silence: “it shall speak.” What comfort it will speak to the believing ear! No promise of his will need to be renewed like a bill that couldn’t be paid on the day it fell due: “it will not tarry.”
Come, my soul, can’t you wait for your God? Rest in him, and be still in a peace too deep for words.

notes.term: The vision is yet for an appointed time
notes.note: God’s answer to Habakkuk, who had asked how long evil would go unpunished ([[Hab.2.3|Habakkuk 2:3]]).
Goings out; the moments when his power goes into action.
A law or promise still on the books that no longer has any force.
A written promise to pay a sum of money on a set date. If it couldn’t be paid when due, it had to be renewed for a later date.
Delay, linger.
Too deep for words.

modern: Three armies were dying of thirst, and the Lord stepped in. Though he sent neither cloud nor rain, he still supplied plenty of water. He doesn’t depend on ordinary methods, but can surprise his people with new displays of wisdom and power. In this way we’re made to see more of God than ordinary processes could have shown us. Though the Lord may not come to our help in the way we expect or want or imagine, he will provide for us in one way or another. It’s a great blessing to be lifted above looking to secondary causes, so that we can gaze into the face of the great First Cause.

Do we have enough grace today to dig trenches for God’s blessing to flow into? Sadly, we too often fail to show true, practical faith. Let’s be on the lookout today for answers to prayer. Like the child who went to a meeting to pray for rain and took her umbrella with her, let’s truly and practically expect the Lord to bless us. Let’s fill the valley with ditches, and expect to see every one of them filled.

notes.term: Make this valley full of ditches
notes.note: Elisha’s word to the kings of Israel, Judah and Edom, whose armies had run out of water on the way to fight Moab. The next morning water came and filled the land ([[2Kgs.3.16-2Kgs.3.20|2 Kings 3:16–20]]).
Stepped in.
The ordinary means God works through, such as weather, people and events, as distinct from God himself, the First Cause behind them all.
An old cry of sorrow or regret.
Showing, display.

modern: Our heavenly Father wants to instruct us, not destroy us. His contending with us has a kind intention toward us. He won’t always be up in arms against us. We think the Lord is long in his discipline, but that’s because we are short in our patience. His compassion lasts forever, but his quarrel with us doesn’t. The night may drag on its weary length, but in the end it must give way to cheerful day. Just as the quarrel lasts only for a season, so the anger behind it lasts only for a small moment. The Lord loves his chosen too much to be angry with them forever.

If he dealt with us always the way he does sometimes, we would faint completely and go down without hope to the gates of death. Take courage, dear heart! The Lord will soon stop scolding. Bear up, for the Lord will bear you up and bear you through. He who made you knows how frail you are and how little you can bear. He will handle tenderly what he has made so delicately. So don’t be afraid because of the painful present, for it is hurrying on to a happy future. He who struck you will heal you; his little anger will be followed by great mercies.

notes.term: I will not contend for ever

notes.note: Quarrel, strive against.
Discipline, correction.
“In a little wrath I hid my face from thee for a moment; but with everlasting kindness will I have mercy on thee” ([[Isa.54.7-Isa.54.8|Isaiah 54:7–8]]).
Scolding.

notes.term: He that smote you will heal you
notes.note: Smote means struck. “He hath smitten, and he will bind us up” ([[Hos.6.1|Hosea 6:1]]).

modern: Delight in God has a transforming power. It lifts a person above the crude desires of our fallen nature. Delight in Jehovah is not only sweet in itself; it sweetens the whole soul, until the heart’s longings become such that the Lord can safely promise to fulfill them. Isn’t that a grand delight, which shapes our desires until they are like the desires of God?

Our foolish way is to want something and then set to work to get what we want. We don’t go about it God’s way, which is to seek him first and then expect all things to be added to us. If we’ll let our heart be filled with God until it runs over with delight, then the Lord himself will make sure we don’t lack any good thing. Instead of going out looking for joys, let’s stay at home with God, and drink water from our own fountain. He can do far more for us than all our friends. It’s better to be content with God alone than to go around fretting and pining for the cheap trifles of this passing world. For a while we may have disappointments; but if they bring us nearer to the Lord, they are to be prized very highly, for in the end they will secure for us the fulfillment of all our right desires.

notes.term: Delight thyself also in the Lord

notes.note: Coarse, crude.
The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Bring about, get.

notes.term: All things to be added unto us
notes.note: “Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you” ([[Matt.6.33|Matthew 6:33]]).
Away from home; out and about.

notes.term: Drink waters out of our own fountain
notes.note: “Drink waters out of thine own cistern, and running waters out of thine own well” ([[Prov.5.15|Proverbs 5:15]]).
This passing world, and the things the senses can reach, as opposed to eternal things seen by faith.

modern: It shouldn’t be hard for us to humble ourselves, for what do we have to be proud of? We should take the lowest place without being told to. If we are sensible and honest, we’ll be small in our own eyes. Before the Lord in prayer especially, we’ll shrink to nothing. There we can’t speak of merit, for we have none; our one and only appeal must be to mercy: “God be merciful to me a sinner.”

Here is a cheering word from the throne. We’ll be lifted up by the Lord if we humble ourselves. For us, the way up is downhill. When we are stripped of self we are clothed with humility, and that is the best thing to wear. The Lord will lift us up in peace and happiness of mind; he will lift us up into knowledge of his Word and fellowship with himself; he will lift us up in the enjoyment of sure pardon and justification. The Lord puts his honors on those who can wear them to the honor of the Giver. He gives usefulness, acceptance and influence to those who won’t be puffed up by them, but humbled by a sense of greater responsibility. Neither God nor man will care to lift up a man who lifts himself up; but God and good people join together to honor modest worth.
O Lord, sink me low in myself, so that I may rise in you.

notes.term: He that humbleth himself shall be exalted
notes.note: The last words of Jesus’ parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector ([[Luke.18.9-Luke.18.14|Luke 18:9–14]]).

notes.term: God be merciful to me a sinner
notes.note: The tax collector’s prayer ([[Luke.18.13|Luke 18:13]]).
Lifted up; raised to honor.
“Be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble” ([[1Pet.5.5|1 Peter 5:5]]).
The best clothing there is.
God declaring a sinner righteous for Christ’s sake.
Humbled, brought low.

modern: We should value our weakness, because it makes room for God’s strength. We might never have known the power of grace if we hadn’t felt the weakness of nature. Blessed be the Lord for the thorn in the flesh and the messenger of Satan, when they drive us to the strength of God.

This is a precious word from our Lord’s own lips. It has made the writer laugh for joy. God’s grace enough for me! I should think it is! Isn’t the sky enough for the bird, and the ocean enough for the fish? The All-Sufficient is sufficient for my greatest need. He who is sufficient for earth and heaven is certainly able to meet the case of one poor worm like me.

So let’s fall back on our God and his grace. If he doesn’t take away our grief, he will enable us to bear it. His strength will be poured into us until the worm threshes the mountains, and a nobody conquers all the high and mighty. It’s better for us to have God’s strength than our own; for if we were a thousand times as strong as we are, it would all come to nothing in the face of the enemy; and if we could be weaker than we are, which is hardly possible, we could still do all things through Christ.

notes.term: My grace is sufficient for thee
notes.note: The Lord’s answer when Paul prayed three times for his “thorn in the flesh” to be taken away ([[2Cor.12.8-2Cor.12.9|2 Corinthians 12:8–9]]).

notes.term: The thorn in the flesh, and the messenger of Satan
notes.note: Paul’s words for a trouble he never names: “a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me” ([[2Cor.12.7|2 Corinthians 12:7]]).
God, who is everything we need; a meaning often given for his name El Shaddai, “God Almighty”.
Need.

notes.term: The worm shall thresh the mountains
notes.note: “Fear not, thou worm Jacob… thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small” ([[Isa.41.14-Isa.41.15|Isaiah 41:14–15]]).
“I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me” ([[Phil.4.13|Philippians 4:13]]).

modern: Being the Lord’s own people is a choice blessing, but knowing that we are is a comforting blessing. It’s one thing to hope that God is with us, and another to know that he is. Faith saves us, but assurance satisfies us. We take God as our God when we believe in him; but we get the joy of him when we know that he is ours and we are his. No believer should be content with hoping and trusting; he should ask the Lord to lead him on to full assurance, so that the things he hopes for become things he is certain of.

It’s when we enjoy the blessings of the covenant, and see our Lord Jesus raised up for us as a plant of renown, that we come to know clearly God’s favor toward us. We learn that we are the Lord’s people not by law but by grace. Let’s always turn our eyes in the direction of free grace. Assurance of faith can never come by the works of the law. It’s a gospel virtue, and it can only reach us in a gospel way. Let’s not look inside ourselves. Let’s look to the Lord alone. As we see Jesus, we’ll see our salvation.
Lord, send us such a flood tide of your love that we’re washed up beyond the mud of doubt and fear.

notes.term: Thus shall they know that I the Lord their God am with them
notes.note: [[Ezek.34.30|Ezekiel 34:30]], the end of God’s promise to shepherd his scattered flock himself.
In older English, comforting and strengthening.
Being fully sure that you belong to God. “Let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith” ([[Heb.10.22|Hebrews 10:22]]).
“I will raise up for them a plant of renown” ([[Ezek.34.29|Ezekiel 34:29]]), read as a promise of Christ. Renown means fame.
Belonging to the gospel. (“Evangel” is an old word for gospel.)
The incoming tide at its height.
Deep mud.

modern: If the Lord won’t allow it, neither people nor devils can do it. How they would rejoice if they could give us a disgraceful fall, drive us from our position and bury us out of memory! They could do all this to their heart’s content if it weren’t for one obstacle, and only one: the Lord won’t allow it. And if he won’t allow it, we won’t have to suffer it.

The way of life is like traveling in the Alps. Along mountain paths your foot is always in danger of slipping. Where the path is high, your head is apt to spin, and then your feet soon slide. There are places as smooth as glass and others rough with loose stones, and on either one a fall is hard to avoid. Whoever is enabled all through life to keep upright and walk without stumbling has the best of reasons to be grateful. With pitfalls and snares, weak knees, weary feet and cunning enemies, no child of God would stand firm for an hour if it weren’t for the faithful love that won’t let his foot be moved. “Amidst a thousand snares I stand Upheld and guarded by thy hand; That hand unseen shall hold me still, And lead me to thy holy hill.”

notes.term: He will not suffer thy foot to be moved
notes.note: [[Ps.121.3|Psalm 121:3]]. In older English, “suffer” means allow. Spurgeon plays on both senses: if the Lord won’t allow it, we won’t have to undergo it.
Obstacle.
Likely to spin, as when you feel dizzy.
Cunning, crafty.
Zion, where God dwells; here, heaven. “Let them bring me unto thy holy hill” ([[Ps.43.3|Psalm 43:3]]).

modern: Sin will reign if it can: it can’t be satisfied with any place lower than the throne of the heart. Sometimes we fear it will conquer us, and then we cry to the Lord, “Let not any iniquity have dominion over me.” This is his comforting answer: “Sin shall not have dominion over you. It may attack you, and even wound you; but it will never set up its rule over you.”

If we were under the law, our sin would gather strength and keep us under its power; for it’s the punishment of sin that a person comes under the power of sin. Since we are under the covenant of grace, we are kept safe from turning away from the living God by the covenant’s sure promise. Grace is promised to us, and by it we are brought back from our wanderings, cleansed from our impurities and set free from the chains of habit.

We might lie down in despair and be “content to serve the Egyptians” if we were still slaves working for eternal life; but since we are the Lord’s free men, we take courage to fight our corruptions and temptations, sure that sin will never bring us under its power again. God himself gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.

notes.term: Sin shall not have dominion over you
notes.note: [[Rom.6.14|Romans 6:14]]. Dominion means rule.

notes.term: Let not any iniquity have dominion over me
notes.note: [[Ps.119.133|Psalm 119:133]]. Iniquity means wickedness.
Attack.
God’s binding promise to save his people through Christ, freely, as a gift and not a reward.
At the Red Sea, the frightened Israelites told Moses, “Let us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians” ([[Exod.14.12|Exodus 14:12]]).
The sinful desires still at work in a believer.
Rule, control.

notes.term: God Himself giveth us the victory
notes.note: “Thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ” ([[1Cor.15.57|1 Corinthians 15:57]]).

modern: Notice the “my” that comes twice: “My people shall be satisfied with my goodness.”

The kind of people who are satisfied with God are marked out as God’s own. He is pleased with them, for they are pleased with him. They call him their God, and he calls them his people. He is satisfied to take them as his portion, and they are satisfied with him as their portion. There is a shared fellowship of delight between God’s Israel and Israel’s God.

These people are satisfied. This is a grand thing. Very few people are ever satisfied, whatever their lot may be; they have swallowed the horseleech, and it keeps crying, “Give! Give!” Only sanctified souls are satisfied souls. God himself must both convert us and content us.

It’s no wonder that the Lord’s people are satisfied with the goodness of their Lord. Here is goodness with nothing mixed in, generosity without limit, mercy without scolding, love without change, favor without holding back. If God’s goodness doesn’t satisfy us, what will? What! Are we still groaning? Surely there’s a wrong desire inside us if it’s one God’s goodness doesn’t satisfy.
Lord, I am satisfied. Blessed be your name.

notes.term: My people shall be satisfied with my goodness
notes.note: [[Jer.31.14|Jeremiah 31:14]], from God’s promise to bring his people home from exile.
A share of an inheritance. When God is “our portion”, he himself is what we inherit, and he is enough. And “the LORD’s portion is his people” ([[Deut.32.9|Deuteronomy 32:9]]).
Close fellowship and sharing, with God or with each other.
A bloodsucking leech. “The horseleach hath two daughters, crying, Give, give” ([[Prov.30.15|Proverbs 30:15]]): a picture of an appetite that is never satisfied.
Make holy; set apart for God.
Generosity.
Limit, holding back.
Scolding.

modern: Jehovah is “the Keeper of Israel.” No kind of unconsciousness ever steals over him, neither the deeper slumber nor the lighter sleep. He never fails to watch over the house and the heart of his people. This is reason enough for us to rest in perfect peace. Alexander said he slept because his friend Parmenio was keeping watch; we have far more reason to sleep, because our God is our guard.

“Behold” is set here to call our attention to this cheering truth. When Israel had a stone for his pillow, he fell asleep; but his God was awake, and came to his servant in a vision. When we lie defenseless, Jehovah himself will cover our head.

The Lord keeps his people as a rich man keeps his treasure, as a captain keeps a city with a garrison, as a sentry keeps watch over his king. No one can harm those who are kept like this. Let me put my soul into his dear hands. He never forgets us, never stops actively caring for us and never finds himself unable to keep us safe.

O my Lord, keep me, so that I don’t wander and fall and perish. Keep me, so that I may keep your commandments. By your unsleeping care, keep me from sleeping like the sluggard, and from perishing like those who sleep the sleep of death.

notes.term: He that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep

notes.note: The personal name of God in the Old Testament, printed “the LORD” in most English Bibles.
Alexander the Great and Parmenio, his most trusted general.

notes.term: Israel… a stone for his pillow
notes.note: Jacob, later named Israel, slept on a stone at Bethel and dreamed of a ladder to heaven, with the Lord standing above it ([[Gen.28.11-Gen.28.13|Genesis 28:11–13]]).
“Thou hast covered my head in the day of battle” ([[Ps.140.7|Psalm 140:7]]).
Troops stationed in a town to defend it.
The lazy man of Proverbs: “How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard?” ([[Prov.6.9|Proverbs 6:9]]).
“Lighten mine eyes, lest I sleep the sleep of death” ([[Ps.13.3|Psalm 13:3]]).

modern: What a wide promise! Anything! Whether large or small, all my needs are covered by that word “anything.” Come, my soul, be free at the mercy-seat, and hear your Lord saying to you, “Open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it.”

What a wise promise! We are always to ask in the name of Jesus. While this encourages us, it also honors him. This is a plea that never runs out. Sometimes every other plea is clouded, especially those we could draw from our own relationship to God or our experience of his grace; but at such times the name of Jesus is as mighty at the throne as ever, and we can plead it with full assurance.

What an instructive prayer! I may not ask for anything that I can’t put Christ’s hand and seal to. I don’t dare use my Lord’s name on a selfish or willful request. I may only use my Lord’s name on prayers he would pray himself if he were in my situation. It’s a high privilege to be authorized to ask in the name of Jesus, as if Jesus himself were asking; but our love for him will never let us put that name where he wouldn’t have put it.
Am I asking for something Jesus approves? Do I dare put his seal to my prayer? Then I have what I am asking the Father for.

notes.term: If ye shall ask anything in my name, I will do it

notes.note: The gold lid of the ark of the covenant, where God met with his people; a picture of coming to God in prayer.

notes.term: Open thy mouth wide, and I will fill it

notes.note: An argument or reason put forward when asking for something.
A signature and a wax seal, which made a document official.
A request.
